adversarial_test_results.prompt: The boats came back to the bay after dark, and the crew stacked the wet nets on the dock while a lamp swung over the water and the birds called from the rocks.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The old dog began to bay at the moon, and the farmer switched on the porch light to see what had made the noise.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The token ' bay' is a complete one-token word in its verb sense, chunk-final within the clause, which the hypothesis says fires weakly.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The path from the lodge to the river was muddy after the rain, so we carried our boots and walked slowly past the empty fields.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The token ' to' appears only as an ordinary preposition between two plain nouns, a compositional use the hypothesis calls broken and therefore weak, and the driver token 'Road' from example 2 is replaced by a common noun.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She wanted to leave early, but the manager asked her to stay and finish the report before the office closed for the long weekend.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Both ' to' tokens are infinitival markers in ordinary clauses, not parts of any conventionalized name, title, idiom or compound, so the hypothesis predicts weak firing.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: He drew a path to nowhere on the back of a menu, then laughed and crossed it out with a pen before the waiter came back.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The token ' to' sits inside a novel non-conventionalized phrase that merely resembles the shape of the example title, the broken-unit case the hypothesis says fires weakly.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: He crossed the line first, then sat on the grass and waited for the others to finish the last stretch of the race.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The token ' first' is a single-token adverb that ends its clause, the chunk-final case the hypothesis explicitly predicts fires weakly.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The teacher handed out a sheet with ten questions, and the first one asked the class to circle the best answer in each row.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The token ' first' is a compositional ordinal in a plain noun phrase, and the unit it would belong to (the ordinal plus its noun) is not a conventionalized multi-token unit, so the hypothesis predicts weak firing.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The price of milk went up again last month, and the shop raised the cost by ten cents a bottle.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The token ' up' is a single complete token closing a phrasal verb, chunk-final, which the hypothesis predicts fires weakly.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The plane left the gate an hour late, and the flight was rough for most of the way to the coast before it cleared.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The claimed token ' flight' is a single complete token heading its own phrase with no multi-token unit still underway, so the hypothesis predicts weak firing at it.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The part of the wall near the window was damp, so the painter wiped it and put on a fresh coat of white paint.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tokens from the WordNet sibling categories ' part' and ' wall' occur as complete single tokens carrying none of the claimed non-final-unit feature, so the hypothesis predicts no firing.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The gallery hung her art above the fireplace, and visitors stood there for a long time before moving to the next room.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The claimed token ' art' is a single complete token with nothing of a unit following it, which the hypothesis says fires weakly.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Our neighbor Art brought a salad to the picnic and told the same story twice while the kids played near the trees.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A proper name is present, but ' Art' is a single complete token, so the name is chunk-final at that token and the hypothesis predicts weak firing even for a proper name.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The agency said research spending in Canada rose again last year, and it published the figures in March to little notice.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Same topic and vocabulary as example 1 (research and development spending in Canada) with every token a complete single word from the first position on, and no non-final part of any name, title, idiom, compound or long word, so the hypothesis predicts no firing.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: He wrote road on one line, to on the next, and recovery below that, then asked what the program was meant to do.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The example's title tokens appear as three separate complete tokens broken apart by syntax, the broken-unit case the hypothesis says fires weakly rather than as a title underway.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The desert is dry, and rain has never been recorded there in living memory, even in the wet season.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Same topic as example 4 (desert, rain never recorded) built entirely from complete single tokens with no name, title, idiom, compound or long-word chunk, so the hypothesis predicts no firing.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The cabin had no AC, so we slept on the porch and woke at dawn when the birds began to sing.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The claimed surface token ' AC' is a complete single token abbreviation rather than a non-final chunk of a longer word, so the hypothesis predicts weak firing.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The bus stopped at the corner, and a woman in a blue coat got off with two bags of food from the market.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Control negative of complete single tokens: there is no claimed trigger token and no non-final part of any multi-token unit, so the hypothesis predicts no firing.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The meeting ran late, and everyone left the room without saying much, so the corridor was quiet by eight.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Second control negative of complete single tokens with no claimed trigger and no unit underway, so the hypothesis predicts no firing.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Park staff said the trail would open again once crews cleared the fallen trees, and visitors should check the website for news.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Same topic and vocabulary as example 2 (park, visitors, updates) with the title removed and every token complete, so the hypothesis predicts no firing and this separates the feature from the topic.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The kitchen was quiet in the early morning, and the light came in through the window over the sink. She filled the kettle and set it on the stove, then wiped the table with a cloth. Outside, a van stopped at the corner and a man carried boxes up the steps of the house across the street. The kettle began to sing, and she poured the water slowly into a cup while the radio played a song she did not know.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Long-context negative matched in length to the long holdout: every token is a complete common word, with no proper name, title, idiom, hyphenated compound or multi-token long word, so the hypothesis predicts no firing anywhere in the passage.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She moved to New York City in the spring and found work at a small press near the river, where she still lives.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive holdout: ' New' and ' York' are non-final tokens of the conventionalized proper name 'New York City', the claimed feature in a new context with none of the example's trigger words.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The ambulance arrived in the nick of time, and the boy was rushed to the hospital where the doctors were waiting.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive holdout: ' nick' is a non-final token of the fixed idiom 'in the nick of time', a unit type the hypothesis lists, expressed with vocabulary absent from the examples.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The trial used a double-blind design, so neither the patients nor the doctors knew who received the drug until the end.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive holdout: ' double' followed by the hyphen and 'blind' is the non-final part of a hyphenated compound, which the hypothesis lists as an activating unit type.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The capital of Norway has more electric cars per person than any other city in Europe, according to a recent survey.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive holdout: ' capital' heads a noun-plus-complement construction whose complement is still to come, the unit type the hypothesis names, with no claimed trigger token present.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The Industrial Revolution began in a few valleys, and its effects took a century to reach the coast.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive holdout: ' Indust' is a measured non-final chunk of the long word 'Industrial', and the same token is the non-final part of the conventionalized name 'Industrial Revolution', so both the long-word and proper-name clauses of the hypothesis predict firing there.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The undersigned parties agree that the arbitration clause survives the termination of this agreement and remains in force.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Cross-genre positive holdout from legal prose: ' unders' is the non-final first chunk of the long word 'undersigned', exactly the mid-word position the hypothesis says fires.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The firm reported strong first-quarter earnings and raised its outlook for the year, sending the shares higher on Monday.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive holdout in a business register: ' first' followed by the hyphen is the non-final part of the hyphenated compound 'first-quarter', which the hypothesis predicts fires, in contrast with the chunk-final negatives.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: El equipo viajó a Buenos Aires para disputar la final del campeonato nacional ante miles de aficionados.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Cross-language positive holdout: 'Buenos' is a non-final token of the conventionalized proper name 'Buenos Aires', the claimed feature in Spanish.

adversarial_test_results.detail: Cross-language positive holdout in the script of the Hebrew examples: a conventionalized proper name and a fixed institutional collocation are underway mid-sentence, which the hypothesis predicts fires whatever the language.
